title: Design Removable Queue
description:
Design a FIFO queue `RemovableQueue` of unique integer IDs that also supports `O(1)` cancellation of any ID currently waiting in the queue:
- `RemovableQueue()` initializes an empty queue.
- `boolean enqueue(int id)` appends `id` to the back of the queue and returns `true` if `id` is not already present; if `id` is already in the queue, does nothing and returns `false`.
- `int dequeue()` removes and returns the front `id` of the queue, or returns `-1` if the queue is empty.
- `boolean cancel(int id)` removes `id` from anywhere in the queue and returns `true`, or returns `false` if `id` is not currently in the queue.
- `int peekFront()` returns the front `id` without removing it, or `-1` if the queue is empty.
- `int size()` returns the current number of elements in the queue.

All operations must run in `O(1)` time.
constraints: At most 2500 calls will be made across all methods.
hints: Store the queued items in a doubly linked list with sentinel `head` and `tail` nodes so adding to the back and removing from the front or middle all take `O(1)` time.
Pair the doubly linked list with a hash map `id -> Node` to check duplicates on `enqueue` and locate the exact node to unlink on `cancel` in `O(1)`.

examples.explanation: Enqueue 10, 20, 30; cancel(20) removes 20 in O(1); dequeue returns 10, then 30, then -1.
Duplicate enqueue(5) returns false; after dequeue() removes 5, enqueue(5) succeeds again.
Canceling a missing ID returns false, and peekFront/dequeue on an empty queue return -1.
